info.title: Kletia Platform API
info.summary: Non-custodial, chain-agnostic intents for EVM networks and Solana.
info.description:
Plan cross-network intents into a DAG of network-bound steps, get unsigned wallet-ready transactions, and verify execution from on-chain evidence. Kletia never holds keys. Networks are CAIP-2 ids, accounts CAIP-10, assets CAIP-19, amounts base-unit strings.

Tiers: public 30/min per IP, developer 300/min per key, operator 1200/min per key. Errors are `{ "error": { "code", "message", "issues"?, "hints"?, "docs"? }, "requestId" }` with codes from the catalog at GET /v1/errors; every response carries X-Request-Id. Keyed POSTs that create or change state accept `Idempotency-Key`. Agents can use the read-only MCP server at /v1/mcp.

post.summary: Best routes for one asset movement (same- or cross-network)
post.description: Quotes are advisory and never persisted. Routes are ranked like the planner's bridge auction (guaranteed output net of priced extra costs, then time within `maxSeconds`, then transaction count); `best` is the first eligible route.

post.summary: Plan an intent into an IntentGraph
post.description: Natural-language `text` is compiled by a deterministic grammar; unsupported wording returns 422 INTENT_UNSUPPORTED with example phrases in `error.hints`. With `dryRun=true` the plan is quoted but not stored (200; Idempotency-Key is ignored). A repeated `clientReference` from the same API key returns the original intent (200). Honours `Idempotency-Key` (with an API key): a retry with the same key and request replays the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

200.description: Dry run, or idempotent replay of an existing intent.

get.summary: List intents created with the caller's key

post.summary: Build wallet-ready transactions for a ready step
post.description: Every transaction is sent (EVM) or fee-paid (Solana) by the step account. Sign and send them in order, then submit the references. A payload expires at `payload.expiresAt`; prepare again to re-quote. Never retried automatically: an `Idempotency-Key` header is refused with 400 IDEMPOTENCY_NOT_SUPPORTED.

post.summary: Submit transaction hashes / signatures for on-chain verification
post.description: A reference advances the step only after Kletia observes it on-chain from the bound account. Same-network steps become `settled`; cross-network steps become `settling` until the settlement network reports the destination fill. References that are provably not this step's transactions are refused with 422 (REFERENCE_WRONG_SENDER, REFERENCE_WRONG_CHAIN, REFERENCE_MISMATCH, REFERENCE_STALE, REFERENCE_ALREADY_USED) and leave the step unchanged. References not yet visible on-chain are stored (`submitted`) and re-verified by refresh and the settlement poller; until one of them produces on-chain evidence, new references (e.g. after a wallet speed-up) replace them. Honours `Idempotency-Key` (with an API key): a retry with the same key and request replays the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

post.summary: Re-read verification and settlement state now
Cancel an intent with no submitted steps

get.summary: Server-Sent Events stream of intent events
get.description: Starts with `retry: 3000`, replays buffered events after `Last-Event-ID` (or `?since=`; the whole buffer when absent, or when the id is no longer buffered, so de-duplicate by event id), then streams live events. Each frame is `id: <event id>`, `event: <type>`, `data: <KletiaEvent JSON>`. A comment heartbeat is sent every 15 s and the stream ends after 30 minutes.

200.description: Event stream. Every `data` line is a KletiaEvent (see components.schemas.KletiaEvent).

text/event-stream.example:
retry: 3000

id: evt_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
event: intent.created
data: {"id":"evt_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","type":"intent.created","at":"2026-10-08T12:00:00.000Z","data":{"intentId":"int_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","summary":{}}}

post.description: At most 10 webhooks per key. Deliveries are signed with `Kletia-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<raw body>")>`; verify with verifyWebhookSignature from @kletia/core. Honours `Idempotency-Key` (with an API key): a retry with the same key and request replays the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. The stored response (with the secret) is encrypted at rest.

delete.summary: Delete a webhook (and its delivery log)

post.summary: Send a signed webhook.test event now
post.description: Makes one synchronous delivery attempt of a `webhook.test` event (see the webhookTest webhook) with the same signing, network rules, 5 s timeout and no-redirect policy as real deliveries, records it in the delivery log and returns the outcome. Always 200 when the attempt was made, whatever the endpoint answered. Test deliveries never pause a webhook. At most 5 per minute per webhook.

get.description: Every attempt, drop and test delivery, newest first. Payloads and error text are never stored. Kept for 7 days (at most 1000 per webhook; 100 with in-memory storage).

post.description: The key is shown once and stored only as a SHA-256 hash. Without a key this starts a new project; with a developer key the new key joins the caller's project (at most 5 active keys, else 409 KEY_LIMIT_REACHED). Limited to 5 keys per hour per IP. Honours `Idempotency-Key` (with an API key): a retry with the same key and request replays the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. The stored response is encrypted at rest.

get.summary: List the keys of the caller's project
get.description: Never returns secrets, only `last4`. Operator keys cannot be listed (409 KEY_NOT_MANAGEABLE); a secret inside its rotation grace window cannot manage keys (403 KEY_SECRET_ROTATED).

post.description: Issues a new secret for an active key of the caller's project. The key id is unchanged, so intents, webhooks and usage stay attached. The previous secret keeps authenticating for `graceSeconds` (default 24 h, at most 7 days, 0 = stop now) but cannot manage keys; rotating again ends an earlier grace window. Other instances notice within 15 s. Honours `Idempotency-Key` (with an API key): a retry with the same key and request replays the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. The stored response is encrypted at rest and replayed only to the current secret or to the secret that made the request (a key that rotated itself can retry with its old secret during the grace window); any other rotated-out secret gets 403 KEY_SECRET_ROTATED.

200.description: The key with its new secret.

delete.summary: Revoke a key of the caller's project
delete.description: Idempotent. The key stops authenticating at once on the answering instance and within 15 s everywhere. A key may revoke itself. Its webhooks and their delivery logs are deleted and its intents' events are no longer delivered; repeating the call finishes a cleanup that failed (503).

get.summary: Requests, status classes and intents of the caller's key
get.description: Counts every request made with the key, by hour, route and status class (flushed every 30 s), plus the live rate-limit window of the answering instance and the intents the key created in the window.
Every error code the API returns, and every step failure code, with its status, category, retryability and remedy. Cacheable for 5 minutes.

operational / degraded / down from the health report. SVG by default; `format=shields` returns a shields.io endpoint document for `https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=<encoded URL>`. Cacheable for 60 seconds.

post.description: MCP revision 2026-07-28, plus stateless serving of 2025-era clients that open with `initialize`. Send one JSON-RPC message per request with `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`; batches are refused and GET answers 405 (no server-initiated stream). Tools, all read-only: `list_networks`, `list_protocols`, `list_assets`, `get_quote`, `plan_intent`, `get_intent`, `list_intents`, `get_portfolio`, `create_signing_link`. No tool prepares, signs or submits a transaction; `create_signing_link` returns a Studio link (text up to 500 characters) for the user to sign with their own wallet. An API key maps to the MCP auth info (`clientId` = key id). Requests with an `Origin` header must come from an HTTPS origin (or localhost in development), else 403 MCP_ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN. Add it to Claude Code with `claude mcp add --transport http kletia https://api.kletiaai.xyz/v1/mcp`.

200.description: JSON-RPC response (application/json), or an event stream for 2025-era requests.

400.description: A JSON-RPC error for a batch, a body that is not one JSON-RPC message, an unsupported protocol revision or MCP headers that disagree with the body; the platform error envelope (INVALID_JSON) for a body that is not JSON.

404.description: A JSON-RPC error (-32601) for an unknown method on the 2026-07-28 revision.

406.description: A JSON-RPC error when Accept does not list both application/json and text/event-stream.

500.description: A JSON-RPC error (-32603) when the MCP server fails; the platform error envelope (INTERNAL_ERROR) for a failure before it.

post.description: Sent for intents created with your API key to each matching webhook. Respond 2xx within 5 seconds; redirects are not followed. Failed deliveries are retried up to 3 times (after 1 s, 5 s and 25 s). Each key's deliveries are queued separately (at most 200 waiting; the oldest is dropped beyond that) and a webhook receives one delivery at a time. A webhook whose last 5 attempts failed is paused for 30 s, doubling up to 5 minutes while it keeps failing; its deliveries wait meanwhile.
Sent once by POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/test, signed like every delivery. Never retried. Acknowledge with any 2xx.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes a retry safe: the first response with this key (per API key) is stored for 24 hours and replayed for the same request. The same key with a different request → 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; while the first request runs → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS (Retry-After: 1; an abandoned reservation is taken over after 120 s). 5xx, 429 and retryable errors are never stored. Requires an API key (400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRES_API_KEY).

X-Request-Id.description: Request id (echoes a valid incoming UUID).

Retry-After.description: Seconds until a retry may succeed.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when the response replays an earlier request (Idempotency-Key or clientReference).

BadRequest.description: Invalid input (INVALID_REQUEST, INVALID_JSON, REFERENCES_INVALID, REFERENCE_INVALID, REFERENCE_COUNT_MISMATCH, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRES_API_KEY, IDEMPOTENCY_NOT_SUPPORTED, ...).

Unauthorized.description: Missing or invalid API key (API_KEY_REQUIRED, INVALID_API_KEY, INVALID_AUTHORIZATION).

NotFound.description: Unknown resource or route (INTENT_NOT_FOUND, STEP_NOT_FOUND, WEBHOOK_NOT_FOUND, KEY_NOT_FOUND, NOT_FOUND).

Conflict.description: State conflict (STEP_NOT_READY, STEP_NOT_AWAITING_SIGNATURE, QUOTE_MOVED, INTENT_CONFLICT, INTENT_NOT_CANCELLABLE, WEBHOOK_EXISTS, KEY_NOT_MANAGEABLE, KEY_LIMIT_REACHED, IDEMPOTENCY_REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS, ...).

Unprocessable.description: Understood but not executable (INTENT_UNSUPPORTED, ROUTE_UNSUPPORTED, CAPITAL_LANE_MIXED, SELF_TRANSFER, FEE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE, WEBHOOK_URL_FORBIDDEN, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, REFERENCE_WRONG_SENDER, REFERENCE_WRONG_CHAIN, REFERENCE_MISMATCH, REFERENCE_STALE, REFERENCE_ALREADY_USED, ...).

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit exceeded (RATE_LIMITED, also for too many unrecognised API keys from one IP; TOO_MANY_STREAMS).

BadGateway.description: An upstream provider or RPC failed (PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, RPC_UNAVAILABLE).

Unavailable.description: Storage or a feature is unavailable (STORE_UNAVAILABLE, also when a presented API key cannot be verified; WEBHOOKS_NOT_CONFIGURED).

GatewayTimeout.description: An upstream provider timed out (UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT, RPC_TIMEOUT).

AssetId.description: CAIP-19 asset id. Natives use `slip44`, ERC-20s `erc20`, SPL mints `token`.

BaseUnits.description: Integer amount in base units, as a string.

DecimalAmount.description: Decimal amount in human units, as a string.

code.description: Stable UPPER_SNAKE_CASE code from the error catalog (GET /v1/errors). Provider failures name the provider (`RELAY_UNAVAILABLE`) and resolve to a catalog family entry.

hints.description: Optional guidance, e.g. example phrases on INTENT_UNSUPPORTED.

status.description: HTTP status when returned as an API error; null when the code only appears as `step.failure.code`.

otherStatuses.description: Statuses the code is also returned with on another path.

retryable.description: True when repeating the same request later can succeed without changing it.

families.description: Dynamic provider codes and the catalog entry describing them.

from.description: Input asset: symbol on `network`, address/mint or CAIP-19 id.

amount.description: Decimal amount of `from`, or `max` (on a dependent step: the guaranteed output of the previous step).

recipient.description: Address or CAIP-10 account. Defaults to the acting account.

deadline.description: Unix seconds after which the plan must not be executed.

maxSeconds.description: Longest settlement estimate a cross-network step may take; slower venue quotes lose the bridge auction.

examples: bridge 25 USDC from base to solana then swap half to JitoSOL

clientReference.description: Idempotency key (honoured for callers with an API key).

quoteBinding.description: SHA-256 binding of the prepared transactions.

to.description: EVM call target; for Solana steps, the program invoked.

recipientName.description: Name the recipient was resolved from (ENS, Basenames, SNS); resolved again before every prepare.

venue.description: Registry venue id (e.g. base:aave-v3:usdc) a deposit or withdraw executes against.

extraCosts.description: Value paid on top of the input, such as a bridge's fixed native fee.

references.description: Submitted transaction hashes / signatures, in order.

EvmTransactionRequest.description: Send with eth_sendTransaction { from, to, data, value } from `from`.

SolanaTransactionRequest.description: Sign and send with the wallet that owns `feePayer` (solana:signAndSendTransaction).

expiresAt.description: Unix seconds; prepare again after this.

actions.description: Action kinds executable with this network as the source.

protocols.description: Registry protocols present on this network.

executable.description: True when the engine has an execution adapter for this protocol.

address.description: ERC-20 contract or SPL mint; null for the native asset.

from.description: Input asset on `network`: symbol, address/mint or CAIP-19 id.

account.description: Sender address or CAIP-10 account (placeholder when omitted).

maxSeconds.description: Longest acceptable settlement estimate; slower routes are not eligible as best.

account.description: Sender address or CAIP-10 account (overrides top-level `account`).

recipient.description: Recipient address or CAIP-10 account (overrides top-level `recipient`).

maxSeconds.description: Longest acceptable settlement estimate; slower routes are not eligible as best.

netMinimumOutput.description: Guaranteed output net of extra costs; absent when those costs cannot be priced.

extraCosts.description: Value paid on top of the input (e.g. a fixed native fee).

eligible.description: False when the route cannot be chosen as best (too slow, unpriced extra costs, another asset).

sealing.description: `development_fallback` (a published key) is only used by development processes with in-memory stores.

pausedWebhooks.description: Webhooks paused after consecutive delivery failures.

secret.description: Signing secret. Returned only by POST /v1/webhooks.

url.description: Public HTTPS endpoint (private, loopback and link-local targets are refused).

key.description: The raw key. Shown once; only its SHA-256 hash is stored.

previousExpiresAt.description: When the previous secret stops authenticating; null when it already has (graceSeconds 0).

graceSeconds.description: How long the previous secret keeps authenticating (it can never manage keys). 0 revokes it immediately.

last4.description: Last four characters of the current secret (null for keys issued before they were recorded).

lastUsedAt.description: Updated at most once a minute.

previousExpiresAt.description: End of the open grace window of the previous secret.

current.description: The key that made this request.

error.description: Failure class (error text and payloads are never stored). `redirect`: a 3xx answer, which is never followed; `queue_full`: dropped before sending.

nextRetryAt.description: When a failed attempt is retried.

since.description: Start of the first hour in the window.

rateLimit.description: The current 1-minute window as seen by the answering instance.

series.description: One entry per hour of the window, oldest first.

intents.description: Intents the key created in the window, by current status.

JsonRpcRequest.description: One MCP JSON-RPC message (batches are refused).

JsonRpcErrorResponse.description: A JSON-RPC error sent with a non-2xx status by the MCP server: the code is a JSON-RPC integer and there is no `requestId` (read the X-Request-Id header).

references.description: One transaction hash (EVM) or signature (Solana) per prepared transaction, in order.

venue.description: Registry venue id, e.g. base:aave-v3:usdc (use as params.venue).

supplyApy.description: Variable supply APY as a fraction (0.045 = 4.5%); advisory, null when unreadable.

apySource.description: `rate`: the current on-chain supply rate; `share-price`: realised share-price growth over apyWindowSeconds.

exitLiquidity.description: Underlying that can leave the venue now.

unavailable.description: Venues whose on-chain reads failed or no longer match the registry.

keys.description: The project's keys, newest first (at most 50).
